Court System     Exercises 
So, You’re Going to Court? 
The law: Since 1946, there has been a law against disparaging trademarks, but the Supreme Court has yet to 
interpret what exactly “disparaging” means. The Patent and Trademark Office decides which names receive 
trademarks and which don’t.  
Imagine the following scenario: You are a member of a Czech band and proud of your Bohemian heritage. You 
decide to name your band the Bohunks. After touring for several years, you discover there is another band 
with the same name. You feel only your band should benefit from the marketing and hard work you’ve put in 
and want to be the only band allowed to call themselves the Bohunks. You apply for a patent and are denied 
because the term is seen as disparaging. You decide to sue.  
Use the following vocabulary to complete the following steps you will go through on your way to get rights to 
your trademark. Since it is a matter of a Federal jurisdiction, you will go to Federal Court. 
Supreme Court, District Court, Court of Appeals, Defendant, Plaintiff, Appellant, Verdict, Appellee,       
Affirm, Reverse, Precedent, Landmark Decision, Remand, Writ of Certiorari, Appeal 
 
1. You file your claim with a _____________________________________.  From here forward, you are 
known as the _______________________ and the USPTO is known as the ________________________. 
2. The judge rules in favor of the USPTO. You do not agree with the ________________________, and would 
like a different outcome.  
3. The next step is to ______________________ the verdict and take the case to the United States 
____________________________________________. 
4. You are no longer known as the Plaintiff, but rather the ________________________________. The 
USPTO is now called the _________________________________. 
5. Instead of 1 judge hearing your case, there are now 3, 6, 9. (circle one) 
6. You are hoping the judges disagree with the previous court’s decision and ___________________ the first 
verdict. If they decide to _____________________ the decision, it will have to go back to district court and 
the whole process starts all over.  
7. The judges agree with the District Court’s decision and _____________________ the initial verdict. You 
still don’t agree with the decision and only have one option remaining. You must file a petition for 
________________________________ and hope that the highest court approves your petition. 
8. The U.S. _____________________________ approved your petition and now 3, 6, 9 (circle one) justices will 
hear your case. If they rule in your favor, the decision will be known as a 
___________________________________ and ________________________ will have been established.   
9. You won your case and are now free to use the term “Bohunk” as you like. The USPTO approved you 
trademark and others will soon cite your case as precedent for further trademark lawsuits.
